t: This is Inner London, the group of boroughs that form the interior of Greater London, surrounded by Outer London. Its origins lie in the bills of mortality, and it became fixed as a statistical area in 1847. It served as an area of local government from 1855 to 1965. Among those who lived in this part of the city was Anna Letitia Le Breton, an English writer who lived from 1808 to 1885. She is best known for publishing the memoirs of her great-aunt, the poet Anna Laetitia Barbauld, and of her aunt, the writer Lucy Aikin.
